title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026 · Gambler edition · By Richard J Diskin Jr

paragraphs: Monday night is final, so all 13 Week 11 games are graded, from Thursday night in Houston to Monday night in Landover, with a Sunday night stop in Mexico City. Every side on the board Monday night was the Commanders +6, and those tickets were losing twice: down 10 late in the first half and down 7 in the third. Drew Stevens kicked five field goals, the last a 26-yarder as time ran out, and Washington won the game outright.

Graded against the opening lines, the Cover Writer went 5-8 against the spread and 8-5 on the over/under. Graded against the closing lines, the Cover Writer went 8-5 against the spread and 9-4 on the over/under.

Every side is graded on the team picked and every over/under on the Over or Under called, once against the opening line and once against the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss, overtime points count, and picks are graded as they stood at kickoff. Monday's game-day line refresh moved every Commanders ticket from 6.5 to 6 and every Under from 52.5 to 54.5, and put Follow The Money on the Over 54.5. Nothing changed after that. Monday night gets the full ride. The rest of the week gets a quick lap, with the plays that swung the tickets.

Opening line: Bengals −1.5, over/under 52.5. Closing line: Bengals −6.5, over/under 54.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Commanders and the Under, projecting Bengals 27, Commanders 23. Final: Bengals 20, Commanders 22. The Commanders won by 2, and the teams scored 42 points.

Every side on the board was the Commanders +6: the Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches. Those same five had the Under 54.5. Follow The Money stayed off the side and took the Over 54.5 in Monday's line refresh. This game opened with the Bengals laying 1.5 and closed with them laying 6.5, so the Washington ticket bought on Monday came with a lot more room than the one bought a week ago.

The first quarter was all punts. Boye Mafe sacked Jayden Daniels three times in the first half, and Cincinnati gave the ball away at its own 45 when Frankie Luvu stopped Joe Burrow for no gain on fourth-and-1. The Bengals broke through in the second. A 15-play, 71-yard drive ended in Evan McPherson's 38-yarder at 6:17. On the next Cincinnati drive, Burrow hit Samaje Perine for 44 yards on third-and-11 and Tee Higgins for a 31-yard touchdown at 1:55. Bengals 10, Commanders 0. The Commanders +6 was losing by 4, and the half was almost gone.

Then came the flag the Washington tickets were begging for. Daniels went 79 yards in 1:43, and a 32-yard throw to Chig Okonkwo got the Commanders to the Cincinnati 6. On second-and-goal from the 5 with 19 seconds left, his pass for Treylon Burks fell incomplete, and Dax Hill was flagged for pass interference. Ball at the 1. Jacory Croskey-Merritt went in on the next snap with 12 seconds left. Bengals 10, Commanders 7 at the half, 17 points. The +6 was covering by 3, and the Under had 37.5 points to play with.

Daniels opened the second half with a 47-yard scramble to the Cincinnati 14, and the drive went backward from there: a false start on Chris Paul, two incompletions, and a 36-yard Stevens field goal at 11:47. Bengals 10, Commanders 10. Cincinnati answered right away. Trey Amos was flagged for pass interference on Ja'Marr Chase, Mike Gesicki caught passes of 19 and 9 yards, and Burrow hit Colbie Young for a 4-yard touchdown at 7:04. Bengals 17, Commanders 10. The +6 was losing again, this time by 1. Stevens hit a 40-yarder at 2:36, and it was Bengals 17, Commanders 13, with the +6 back on top by 2.

The fourth quarter belonged to Stevens and the Under. Myles Murphy jumped offside on third-and-3 at 11:48, and Washington had first-and-goal at the 8. Daniels threw incomplete for Antonio Williams, scrambled for 1, threw incomplete for Stefon Diggs, and Stevens kicked a 25-yarder at 10:32. Bengals 17, Commanders 16, 33 points. On the next Washington drive, a holding flag on Josh Conerly Jr. made it first-and-20, Daniels hit Diggs for 29 yards on second-and-20, and the drive stalled at the 24. Stevens hit from 41 on fourth-and-1 at 2:26. Commanders 19, Bengals 17, 36 points.

Cincinnati had 2:26 to get the lead back, and it did. Gesicki caught a 32-yarder to the Washington 33, Nick Cross and Kain Medrano sacked Burrow on third-and-7, and McPherson drilled a 56-yarder on fourth-and-14 with 46 seconds left. Bengals 20, Commanders 19, 39 points. The Bengals had the lead, and every Commanders +6 ticket was still covering by 5. Follow The Money's Over needed 16 more points in 46 seconds. Daniels hit Antonio Williams for 22 and 42 yards, spiked it at the 8 with 5 seconds left, and Stevens kicked a 26-yarder as time ran out. Commanders 22, Bengals 20, 42 points.

The damage report. Washington won by 2, so the Commanders +6 covered by 8 on the card, by 8.5 at the closing +6.5 and by 3.5 at the opening +1.5. The 42 points stayed under the 54.5 by 12.5. Washington got inside the Cincinnati 20 four times and scored one touchdown, and three of Stevens's five field goals came on those trips. Turn those three kicks into touchdowns and the game lands on 54, still half a point under. Daniels threw for 289 yards and ran for 55, and Antonio Williams caught 9 passes for 122 yards. Burrow threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns, but Cincinnati ran 14 times for 31 yards. Every card that wrote a score had the Bengals winning by 4, and the Commanders won the game by 2.
Missed at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Over, fell short by 10.5 points at the opening 52.5 and fell short by 12.5 points at the closing 54.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Commanders, covered by 3.5 points at the opening Commanders +1.5 and covered by 8.5 points at the closing Commanders +6.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 10.5 points at the opening 52.5 and stayed under by 12.5 points at the closing 54.5.
Follow The Money sat out the side.

Opening line: 49ers −3.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: 49ers −4.5, over/under 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had the 49ers and the Under, projecting 49ers 24, Vikings 19. Final: Vikings 10, 49ers 35. The 49ers won by 25, and the teams scored 45 points.

Letdown Watch was alone on the Vikings +3.5, and that ticket was finished before halftime. Brock Purdy hit Mike Evans for a 4-yard touchdown at 2:09 of the second, and on Minnesota's next snap Ji'Ayir Brown picked off Kirk Cousins and ran it back 18 yards for a touchdown. 49ers 28, Vikings 10. The Under 46.5 was the whole room's sweat. Christian McCaffrey's 6-yard touchdown at 13:26 of the fourth made it 49ers 35, Vikings 10, 45 points. Minnesota got to the San Francisco 20 and came up short on fourth-and-13, then got to the 19 and threw incomplete on fourth-and-8 at 1:52. A field goal on either trip beats the Under. It cashed by 1.5 on the card and by half a point at the closing 45.5.
Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Vikings, missed by 21.5 points at the opening Vikings +3.5 and missed by 20.5 points at the closing Vikings +4.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the 49ers, covered by 21.5 points at the opening 49ers −3.5 and covered by 20.5 points at the closing 49ers −4.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 2.5 points at the opening 47.5 and stayed under by half a point at the closing 45.5.
Follow The Money stayed off the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Broncos −7.5, over/under 41.5. Closing line: Broncos −11.5, over/under 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Raiders and the Over, projecting Broncos 27, Raiders 19. Final: Raiders 24, Broncos 38. The Broncos won by 14, and the teams scored 62 points.

Four cards took the Raiders +10.5, and Letdown Watch laid it with Denver. The Over 41.5 was home at 9:21 of the fourth, when Jonah Coleman's 7-yard touchdown made it Broncos 31, Raiders 17, 48 points. The side went to the wire. The Raiders lost a Jalen Nailor touchdown to an illegal forward pass on Fernando Mendoza, and Jack Bech caught a 7-yard touchdown at 4:29. Broncos 31, Raiders 24, and the Raiders +10.5 was covering by 3.5. Then on third-and-5 at 1:52, Ja'Quan McMillian jumped a throw for Tre Tucker and went 35 yards the other way. Broncos 38, Raiders 24. That pick-six flipped the side, and Letdown Watch cashed on it.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Raiders, missed by 6.5 points at the opening Raiders +7.5 and missed by 2.5 points at the closing Raiders +11.5.

Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Broncos, covered by 6.5 points at the opening Broncos −7.5 and covered by 2.5 points at the closing Broncos −11.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, went over by 20.5 points at the opening 41.5 and went over by 20.5 points at the closing 41.5.
Follow The Money had nothing on the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Jaguars −1.5, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Jaguars −6, over/under 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Giants and the Under, projecting Jaguars 25, Giants 20. Final: Jaguars 18, Giants 23. The Giants won by 5, and the teams scored 41 points.

Four cards took the Giants +6, Next Man Up laid it with Jacksonville, and the whole room had the Under 45.5. New York led 20-6 at the half, so the side was never close. The Under was. Trevor Lawrence hit Brian Thomas Jr. for an 18-yard touchdown at 6:39 of the fourth, and the two-point pass got picked off. Cam Little's 26-yarder at 3:40 made it Giants 23, Jaguars 18, 41 points, and one more Jacksonville touchdown kills the Under. The Jaguars never touched the ball again. Cam Skattebo ran twice for 5 yards each, and J.J. McCarthy knelt it out.
Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Jaguars, missed by 6.5 points at the opening Jaguars −1.5 and missed by 11 points at the closing Jaguars −6.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Giants, covered by 6.5 points at the opening Giants +1.5 and covered by 11 points at the closing Giants +6; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 5.5 points at the opening 46.5 and stayed under by 3.5 points at the closing 44.5.
Follow The Money kept its money off the side.

Opening line: Chargers −9.5, over/under 41.5. Closing line: Chargers −3, over/under 43.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Jets and the Over, projecting Chargers 22, Jets 21. Final: Jets 27, Chargers 24. The Jets won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

Four cards took the Jets +3, Letdown Watch laid it with the Chargers, and In The Trenches left the Over 40.5 for the Under 41.5 on Sunday morning. Geno Smith hit Sterling Shepard for a 16-yard touchdown at 9:46 of the fourth. Jets 27, Chargers 17, 44 points, and the Over 41.5 had cashed. The side got loud late. An illegal use of hands flag on Azareye'h Thomas wiped out a sack, and Ladd McConkey caught a 6-yard touchdown at 1:58. Jets 27, Chargers 24, and Letdown Watch's Chargers −3 needed the ball back and a touchdown. Los Angeles burned all three timeouts, and Braelon Allen ran 15 yards on third-and-7 at 0:47 to end it. The Jets won outright, and the Over In The Trenches walked away from would have cashed by 10.5.

Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Chargers, missed by 12.5 points at the opening Chargers −9.5 and missed by 6 points at the closing Chargers −3; In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 9.5 points at the opening 41.5 and went over by 7.5 points at the closing 43.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Jets, covered by 12.5 points at the opening Jets +9.5 and covered by 6 points at the closing Jets +3; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 9.5 points at the opening 41.5 and went over by 7.5 points at the closing 43.5.
Follow The Money stayed out of the side.

Opening line: Lions −4.5, over/under 49.5. Closing line: Lions −4, over/under 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Lions and the Over, projecting Lions 26, Buccaneers 22. Final: Buccaneers 21, Lions 31. The Lions won by 10, and the teams scored 52 points.

Sunday's refresh moved the Cover Writer and Letdown Watch off the Buccaneers +6.5 and onto the Lions −3.5, where The Formula already was. Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches had the Buccaneers +3.5, and The Formula left the Over 45.5 for the Under 47.5. Tampa had an 80-yard Bucky Irving touchdown wiped out by a holding flag on Luke Goedeke, and it was still Lions 17, Buccaneers 14 going to the fourth. Then the flags turned on Tampa. A face mask on Josiah Trotter set up Jahmyr Gibbs's 1-yard touchdown at 5:24, an unnecessary roughness flag on Vita Vea kept the next Detroit drive alive, and Gibbs scored from 4 yards at 1:55. Lions 31, Buccaneers 14, 45 points. Pass interference flags on Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph moved Tampa down the field, and Baker Mayfield hit Ted Hurst III for a 4-yard touchdown with 8 seconds left. Lions 31, Buccaneers 21, 52 points. That backdoor touchdown cashed the Over and buried The Formula's new Under, and the Buccaneers +6.5 the Cover Writer walked away from would have lost by 3.5.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Buccaneers, missed by 5.5 points at the opening Buccaneers +4.5 and missed by 6 points at the closing Buccaneers +4; The Formula and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 49.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 48.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Lions, covered by 5.5 points at the opening Lions −4.5 and covered by 6 points at the closing Lions −4; The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 49.5 and went over by 3.5 points at the closing 48.5.

Opening line: Ravens −4.5, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Panthers −2.5, over/under 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Ravens and the Over, projecting Panthers 24, Ravens 22. Final: Ravens 33, Panthers 35. The Panthers won by 2, and the teams scored 68 points.

Every side on the board was the Ravens +3, and The Formula and Next Man Up got there in Sunday's refresh by leaving the Panthers −2.5. The Over 43.5 was over at halftime, Ravens 26, Panthers 22, 48 points, so Follow The Money's Under was dead early. The side came down to a flag and a field goal. After Tetairoa McMillan's 7-yard touchdown at 5:06 of the second, an unnecessary roughness flag on Ethan Burke wiped out the extra point, and Carolina went for two and got it. Derrick Henry's 15-yard touchdown at 6:32 of the fourth made it Ravens 33, Panthers 32, and Ryan Fitzgerald's 37-yarder at 1:44 made it Panthers 35, Ravens 33. The Ravens +3 survived by 1, and by half a point at the closing +2.5. Tyrel Dodson picked off Jacoby Brissett at 0:36, and the Panthers −2.5 that The Formula and Next Man Up dropped would have lost by half a point.
Missed at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Under, went over by 21.5 points at the opening 46.5 and went over by 23.5 points at the closing 44.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Ravens, missed by 6.5 points at the opening Ravens −4.5 and covered by half a point at the closing Ravens +2.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, went over by 21.5 points at the opening 46.5 and went over by 23.5 points at the closing 44.5.
Follow The Money wanted no part of the side.

Opening line: Bills −11.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Bills −16.5, over/under 45. The Cover Writer's card had the Dolphins and the Over, projecting Bills 30, Dolphins 17. Final: Dolphins 9, Bills 26. The Bills won by 17, and the teams scored 35 points.

All five cards with a side had the Dolphins +16.5, and five had the Over 44.5. The Over drowned in Josh Allen interceptions, three of them in the last 1:45 of the first half. The side was the sweat of the weekend. Tyler Bass's 40-yarder at 14:56 of the fourth made it Bills 23, Dolphins 9, and the Dolphins +16.5 was covering by 2.5. Buffalo got first-and-goal at the Miami 10 at 2:47, threw incomplete twice, ran for nothing, and sent Bass out for a 28-yarder at 1:57. Bills 26, Dolphins 9, and the +16.5 was losing by half a point. Miami got to the Buffalo 25, where any score covers, and Kyle McCord threw three straight incompletions, the last on fourth-and-9 at 0:25. The Dolphins +16.5 lost by half a point, and Follow The Money's Under cashed.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Dolphins, missed by 5.5 points at the opening Dolphins +11.5 and missed by half a point at the closing Dolphins +16.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 12.5 points at the opening 47.5 and fell short by 10 points at the closing 45.
Called it at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 12.5 points at the opening 47.5 and stayed under by 10 points at the closing 45.
Follow The Money never touched the side.

Opening line: Cowboys −6.5, over/under 48.5. Closing line: Cowboys −7.5, over/under 54.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Titans and the Under, projecting Cowboys 28, Titans 23. Final: Titans 30, Cowboys 51. The Cowboys won by 21, and the teams scored 81 points.

Four cards took the Titans +7.5, Letdown Watch laid it with Dallas, and all five over/under picks were the Under 54.5. Dallas led 27-9 at the half, 36 points. The Under died at 7:19 of the third, when Cam Ward hit Carnell Tate for a 59-yard touchdown. Cowboys 34, Titans 23, 57 points, with a quarter and a half to go. Dak Prescott scored on a challenge, Brandon Aubrey hit from 49, and Quinnen Williams's strip-sack set up another Prescott touchdown pass. Cowboys 51, Titans 30. The whole room's Under lost by 26.5, and Letdown Watch's Cowboys −7.5 never broke a sweat.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Titans, missed by 14.5 points at the opening Titans +6.5 and missed by 13.5 points at the closing Titans +7.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 32.5 points at the opening 48.5 and went over by 26.5 points at the closing 54.5.
Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Cowboys, covered by 14.5 points at the opening Cowboys −6.5 and covered by 13.5 points at the closing Cowboys −7.5.
Follow The Money sat out the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Eagles −5.5, over/under 42.5. Closing line: Steelers −3.5, over/under 37.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Eagles and the Over, projecting Steelers 22, Eagles 19. Final: Steelers 16, Eagles 19. The Eagles won by 3, and the teams scored 35 points.

Five cards had the Eagles +3.5, Next Man Up laid it with Pittsburgh, and five had the Over 37.5 while Follow The Money took the Under. This line opened with the Eagles laying 5.5 and closed with them getting 3.5. It turned into a kicking contest, the last thing an Over ticket wants. A roughing the passer flag on T.J. Watt kept an Eagles drive alive, and Jake Elliott's 55-yarder at 4:19 of the fourth made it Eagles 19, Steelers 9, 28 points. Aaron Rodgers converted a fourth-and-1 himself and hit Max Hurleman for a 20-yard touchdown on third-and-10 at 1:21. Eagles 19, Steelers 16, 35 points. Next Man Up's Steelers −3.5 needed the ball back and a touchdown, and the Over needed 3 more points. Pittsburgh burned all three timeouts, Joe Milton found DeVonta Smith for 7 yards on third-and-6, and Milton knelt it out. The Over fell 2.5 short, and Follow The Money cashed the Eagles and the Under.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 7.5 points at the opening 42.5 and fell short by 2.5 points at the closing 37.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Eagles, missed by 2.5 points at the opening Eagles −5.5 and covered by 6.5 points at the closing Eagles +3.5; Next Man Up on the Steelers, covered by 2.5 points at the opening Steelers +5.5 and missed by 6.5 points at the closing Steelers −3.5.
Called it at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 7.5 points at the opening 42.5 and stayed under by 2.5 points at the closing 37.5.

Opening line: Chiefs −11.5, over/under 44.5. Closing line: Chiefs −15.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Cardinals and the Over, projecting Chiefs 28, Cardinals 18. Final: Cardinals 7, Chiefs 34. The Chiefs won by 27, and the teams scored 41 points.

All five cards with a side had the Cardinals +15.5, and that was gone at the half, Chiefs 27, Cardinals 7. The over/under came down to half a point, and a kick at the end of the half decided it. Patrick Mahomes was flagged for intentional grounding on the last drive of the half, and Harrison Butker hit from 44 as time ran out anyway. Xavier Worthy's 18-yard touchdown at 14:54 of the fourth made it Chiefs 34, Cardinals 7, 41 points, and nobody scored again. Arizona's last real drive lost a 9-yard Tyler Allgeier run to a holding flag on Isaiah Adams and died on downs at the 30. The Over 40.5 cashed by half a point for five cards, and Follow The Money's Under lost by the same half point.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Cardinals, missed by 15.5 points at the opening Cardinals +11.5 and missed by 11.5 points at the closing Cardinals +15.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 3.5 points at the opening 44.5 and went over by half a point at the closing 40.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 3.5 points at the opening 44.5 and went over by half a point at the closing 40.5.
Follow The Money stayed off the side.

Opening line: Bears −6.5, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Bears −11.5, over/under 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Saints and the Under, projecting Bears 28, Saints 20. Final: Saints 13, Bears 21. The Bears won by 8, and the teams scored 34 points.

Four cards took the Saints +11.5, Letdown Watch laid it with Chicago, and the Under 48.5 was never in doubt. The side was, and it turned on a missed extra point. Cairo Santos missed the kick after Colston Loveland's 15-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and when Montez Sweat sacked Tyler Shough for a safety at 12:55 of the fourth, it was Bears 21, Saints 10. With that extra point, Chicago is up 12 and Letdown Watch's Bears −11.5 is covering. The Saints threw incomplete on fourth-and-2 at the Chicago 10 at 8:51, and Charlie Smyth hit a 51-yarder at 1:10. Bears 21, Saints 13. The Saints +11.5 covered by 3.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Saints, missed by 1.5 points at the opening Saints +6.5 and covered by 3.5 points at the closing Saints +11.5; Letdown Watch on the Bears, covered by 1.5 points at the opening Bears −6.5 and missed by 3.5 points at the closing Bears −11.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 12.5 points at the opening 46.5 and stayed under by 13.5 points at the closing 47.5.
Follow The Money kept its money off the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Texans −5.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Texans −12.5, over/under 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Colts and the Over, projecting Texans 26, Colts 20. Final: Colts 3, Texans 26. The Texans won by 23, and the teams scored 29 points.

Five cards took the Colts +12.5, and Follow The Money was alone on the Texans −12.5. In The Trenches had the Under 43.5, and Follow The Money joined it in Thursday morning's refresh. Indianapolis kicked away its chances early. Spencer Shrader missed from 56 and had a 62-yarder blocked by Logan Hall, and it was Texans 17, Colts 3 at the half. One field goal would have put the Colts +12.5 back in front. Will Anderson Jr. sacked Daniel Jones in the end zone for a safety at 10:22 of the third instead, and C.J. Stroud hit Marlin Klein for a 13-yard touchdown at 4:19. Texans 26, Colts 3, 29 points, and Follow The Money cashed both of its tickets.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Colts, missed by 17.5 points at the opening Colts +5.5 and missed by 10.5 points at the closing Colts +12.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Over, fell short by 16.5 points at the opening 45.5 and fell short by 15.5 points at the closing 44.5.

Called it at both numbers: Follow The Money on the Texans, covered by 17.5 points at the opening Texans −5.5 and covered by 10.5 points at the closing Texans −12.5; Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 16.5 points at the opening 45.5 and stayed under by 15.5 points at the closing 44.5.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: Week 11 is closed. The Cover Writer missed 13 times and hit 13 times at the opening lines, and missed 9 times and hit 17 times at the closing lines, with no pushes.

The Cover Writer finished Week 11 at 5-8 against the spread at the open and 8-5 at the close, and 8-5 on the over/under at the open and 9-4 at the close. Monday night went two for two, the Commanders +6 by 8 and the Under 54.5 by 12.5. The best call of the week came at breakfast on Sunday, when leaving the Buccaneers +6.5 for the Lions −3.5 turned a loser into a winner. The worst beat was the Dolphins +16.5, which lost by half a point on a 28-yard chip shot. That one is going on the fridge.

The Formula finished Week 11 at 5-8 against the spread at the open and 8-5 at the close, and 7-6 on the over/under at the open and 8-5 at the close. The Formula cashed both Monday night tickets with the rest of the room. It split its two Sunday morning moves, cashing the Ravens +3 and losing the Under it jumped to in Detroit, where the Over it walked away from cashed. It would like the record to show it was right about Baltimore and would like everyone to stop there.

Next Man Up finished Week 11 at 4-9 against the spread at the open and 5-8 at the close, and 8-5 on the over/under at the open and 9-4 at the close. Next Man Up went solo on the Jaguars −6 and the Steelers −3.5, and both of those teams lost outright. Monday night got it two more winners, and the over/under column was the best part of its week. It is not taking questions about the sides.

Letdown Watch finished Week 11 at 6-7 against the spread at the open and 7-6 at the close, and 8-5 on the over/under at the open and 9-4 at the close. Letdown Watch ran with the pack on Monday night and cashed both. On its own it hit the Broncos on a pick-six with 1:52 left and the Cowboys by 13.5, and it got burned on the Vikings, the Chargers and the Bears. Since opening-line grading began in Week 8 it is 30-26 against the spread at the open, still the only winning side record at the open in the room, and it will bring that up before anybody asks.

Follow The Money finished Week 11 at 1-2 against the spread at the open and 2-1 at the close, and 7-2 on the over/under at the open and 6-3 at the close. Follow The Money took the Over 54.5 on Monday morning and watched Washington kick five field goals. That one lost by 12.5. It still went 7-2 on the over/under at the open this week, and since Week 8 it is 22-8 there, which it brings up every time somebody mentions Monday night.

In The Trenches finished Week 11 at 4-9 against the spread at the open and 7-6 at the close, and 7-6 on the over/under at the open and 8-5 at the close. In The Trenches cashed the Commanders and the Under on Monday night, which helps. It also left the Over 40.5 for the Under 41.5 in Los Angeles on Sunday morning and watched the Jets and Chargers put up 51, and it rode the Under in Detroit into a touchdown with 8 seconds left. The room has asked it to stop touching its tickets on Sunday mornings.

Week 12 starts Wednesday at 8:00 PM ET on Netflix with the Packers at the Rams, and three games land on Thanksgiving. The Commanders, now 4-5-1, visit the Cardinals on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox, and the five cards that rode them Monday night get to find out whether a walk-off field goal is a habit. The Bengals, now 7-3, host the Saints on Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS, and Follow The Money would like a word with Cincinnati's offense before then.
Every card, every game page and every recap lives at thecoverwindow.com.
